title: Towards a Real-Time Vision Correcting Display | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Towards a Real-Time Vision Correcting Display | EECS at UC Berkeley Towards a Real-Time Vision Correcting Display Shiyun Xu EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2022-160 May 20, 2022 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2022/EECS-2022-160.pdf Visual aberrations, such as farsightedness and nearsightedness, have been a prevalent prob- lem around the world for many years. A common way to correct these problems is wearing eyeglasses, which can be cumbersome or infeasible for certain groups of people. An alterna- tive approach is to utilize specialized hardware to convert a normal display to a light-field display and do computation in a specific way such that the displayed image will become clear when it reaches the userâs retina. Recent studies have shown various computing methods on different hardware. However, most of them focus on the quality of the perceived image. In this report, we want to examine these algorithms from a practical point of view, focusing on the tradeoff between runtime and quality. We first propose our design and implementation of two microlens-based prefiltering algorithms and then speed up a few selected algorithms via parallelism to achieve real-time performance.
